questions.solution_text:
Case 1: $x \ge \dfrac{5}{3}$
$3x - 5 \le x + 1 \implies 2x \le 6 \implies x \le 3$
Interval: $\dfrac{5}{3} \le x \le 3$.
Case 2: $x < \dfrac{5}{3}$
$-(3x - 5) \le x + 1 \implies -3x + 5 \le x + 1 \implies -4x \le -4 \implies x \ge 1$
Interval: $1 \le x < \dfrac{5}{3}$.
Combining cases:
$1 \le x \le 3$

questions.solution_text:
Restriction: $x \neq 5$.
Multiply by $6|x - 5| > 0$:
$x|x - 5| \ge 6$
Case 1: $x > 5$
$x(x - 5) \ge 6 \implies x^2 - 5x - 6 \ge 0 \implies (x - 6)(x + 1) \ge 0$
Since $x > 5$, this gives $x \ge 6$.
Case 2: $x < 5$
$-x(x - 5) \ge 6 \implies -x^2 + 5x \ge 6 \implies x^2 - 5x + 6 \le 0 \implies (x - 2)(x - 3) \le 0$
This gives $2 \le x \le 3$.
Combining cases:
$2 \le x \le 3$ or $x \ge 6$

questions.solution_text:
$-10 < x + \dfrac{9}{x} < 10$ with $x \neq 0$.
Case 1: $x > 0$
$x^2 + 9 < 10x \implies x^2 - 10x + 9 < 0 \implies (x - 1)(x - 9) < 0 \implies 1 < x < 9$.
Case 2: $x < 0$
$x + \dfrac{9}{x} > -10 \implies x^2 + 9 < -10x \implies x^2 + 10x + 9 < 0 \implies (x + 1)(x + 9) < 0 \implies -9 < x < -1$.
Combining cases:
$-9 < x < -1$ or $1 < x < 9$
